quote: Our standard practice is to have the Major [release](https://about.gitlab.com/releases/) every May
fact: GitLab's major release (the XX.0 milestone) happens every May, so milestone XX.11 falls in April.

quote: Set the end date to be the Friday prior to the third Thursday of the release month
fact: A product milestone ends on the Friday before the third Thursday of the release month.

quote: All product features must solve an internal use-case/demand first unless it meets a unique strategic advantage and is done in partnership with a particular customer/market vertical.
fact: Under Customer 0, every product feature must first solve an internal use case, unless it has a unique strategic advantage and is built with a particular customer or vertical.

quote: While the Customer 0 model is relevant for the **ideation, development and launch of new features**, dogfooding takes over **once these features are part of our product**.
fact: Customer 0 covers ideation, development and launch of new features; dogfooding applies once the feature is part of the product.

quote: We define specific DRIs in the [categories.yml](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/www-gitlab-com/edit/master/data/categories.yml) file.
fact: Internal Customer DRIs for dogfooding are recorded in the categories.yml file.

quote: We calculated this value by multiplying their responses (1-5) for how efficient they felt a sensing mechanism was by how their responses (1-4) for how effective they felt the sensing mechanism was.
fact: In the 2020 sensing mechanism survey, each mechanism's value was efficiency (1-5) multiplied by effectiveness (1-4).

quote: The CEO is the DRI for pricing and tiers.
fact: The CEO is the directly responsible individual for pricing and tier decisions.

quote: Free is targeted at individual contributor developers. It is a complete DevOps solution and contains capabilities from all ten GitLab stages.
fact: The Free tier targets individual contributor developers and includes capabilities from all ten GitLab stages.

quote: Ultimate is targeted at Executive level buyers and is for organizations.
fact: The Ultimate tier targets executive-level buyers (Premium targets director-level buyers).

quote: With pressure from the market that our SAST features were just open source tools and any customer could just run those themselves for free, we moved SAST analyzers to core.
fact: GitLab moved SAST analyzers to the core (free) tier because the market said they were just open source tools customers could run for free.

quote: Add Product Operations DRI/Maintainer `@fseifoddini` as Reviewer for collaboration and approval.
fact: Changes to the PM SAFE guidance page must be reviewed by Product Operations maintainer @fseifoddini (backup @gweaver), and stay aligned with Legal.

quote: Yes. Whether in epics, issues or handbook pages, PIs should be internal-only and follow the [SAFE framework](/handbook/legal/safe-framework/).
fact: Product performance indicators must be internal-only wherever they appear and follow the Legal SAFE framework.

quote: If an issue with a prioritization label remains without a milestone or planning label after 5 business days, relevant team members receive a reminder
fact: A triage bot reminds team members if a customer-prioritized issue has no milestone or planning label after 5 business days.

quote: **`ProductName::Blocker`** - Cannot sell customer the SKU without this capability
fact: The Blocker label means the customer cannot be sold the SKU without the capability; Retention means they would not stay; Fast Follow means delivery was committed.

quote: **Never include Net ARR, contract values, or revenue figures** in the issue comment
fact: Customer prioritization comments must never contain Net ARR, contract values or revenue figures; those stay in Salesforce.

quote: You do not need to follow the NPI process to launch features into our existing product set and tiers.
fact: Features that fit existing tiers (free, premium, ultimate) do not use the New Product Introduction process; they ship in a release milestone.

quote: Contact Justin Farris's [EBA](/handbook/eba/#executive-business-administrator-team) to schedule time with the Pricing Committee (currently Sean Hall and Justin Farris)
fact: The Pricing Committee is Sean Hall and Justin Farris, scheduled through Justin Farris's executive business admin.

quote: To meet with the SteerCo, reach out to Natalie Pinto or Lee Work who will add you to the next meeting.
fact: To get on the NPI Steering Committee agenda, contact Natalie Pinto or Lee Work.

quote: Any borrow more than 3 months should be reviewed carefully for scope and minimized to the extent possible.
fact: Borrows of team members longer than 3 months get careful scope review; beyond about 6 months a realignment is generally used instead.

quote: the teams who are giving shall have at least 3 engineers remaining and a maximum of 1 engineer can be given
fact: A team giving engineers in a borrow must keep at least 3 engineers and can give at most 1.

quote: A scope reassignment is used when the features or effort of work will take longer than 6 months and less than a year
fact: A scope reassignment is used for work lasting between 6 months and a year, without changing reporting lines.

quote: The Rapid Action process has been replaced by the [Strategic Priority Codes](/handbook/engineering/workflow/strategic-priority-codes/) framework
fact: The Rapid Action process was replaced by the Engineering Strategic Priority Codes framework.

quote: [Gifox](https://gifox.app/) is the absolute best option here, although a paid app, its reasonably priced ($14.99).
fact: The recommended all-in-one GIF tool on macOS is Gifox, a paid app costing $14.99.

quote: It should not require much planning and is typically short in duration (less than 5 min.).
fact: A speed run video is informal, focuses on one workflow and is usually under 5 minutes.

quote: Company targets for our SUS score are: 73 by Q4-FY24, 77 by Q4-FY25, and 82 by Q4-FY26.
fact: The company SUS score targets are 73 by Q4-FY24, 77 by Q4-FY25 and 82 by Q4-FY26.

quote: We use a minimum threshold of 10 product events across at least 2 stages in the previous 30 days.
fact: To be invited to the SUS survey a user needs at least 10 product events across at least 2 stages in the last 30 days.

quote: Those that complete the survey are entered into a quarterly sweepstakes to win one of three $200 gift cards.
fact: SUS respondents enter a quarterly sweepstakes for one of three $200 gift cards, run under Legal's promotional games workflow.

quote: Consider refreshing the UX Scorecard every 6 months, or after significant changes or improvements are made.
fact: UX Scorecards should be refreshed about every 6 months or after significant changes.

quote: Forums are scheduled every two weeks. They are 60 minutes long to allow up to three team members to share for 15 minutes, plus 5 minutes of discussion time with the attendees.
fact: The Upstream Forum runs every two weeks for 60 minutes, with up to three speakers getting 15 minutes each plus 5 minutes of discussion.

quote: Think Big meetings should be conducted in groups of no more than 10-15 (to encourage participation).
fact: Think Big meetings (held once a milestone) should have no more than 10-15 people.

quote: You should keep the RDS team to around 5-7 people.
fact: A Remote Design Sprint team should be about 5-7 people, and the sprint should last two weeks or less.

quote: |  Maximize my confidence when checking that new code is working as expected in production.  |  11.76  |
fact: The top opportunity for the Code Author job performer (validated FY24Q4) scored 11.76: confidence that new code works in production.

quote: The originally planned FY2026 Q3 collection was skipped due to a need to prioritize other surveys.
fact: The FY2026 Q3 USAT+ survey collection was skipped to prioritize other surveys.

quote: Eligible users are invited through email waves of approximately 5,000 users each, scheduled Monday-Friday at 8-9am Eastern Time to maximize visibility.
fact: USAT+ invites go out in email waves of about 5,000 users, weekdays at 8-9am Eastern.

quote: 1:5 ratio of UX Researchers to Product Managers
fact: Headcount planning uses one UX Researcher per five Product Managers.

quote: The Product Manager for [Growth: Engagement](/handbook/product/categories/#engagement-group) is the [DRI](/handbook/people-group/directly-responsible-individuals/#what-is-a-directly-responsible-individual) for navigation changes.
fact: The Growth: Engagement Product Manager is the DRI for navigation changes.

quote: If at any point you notice that less than 80% of participants are able to pass a scenario, the study should stop at that most recent participant to conserve resources.
fact: A Category Maturity Scorecard study stops early if fewer than 80% of participants pass a scenario.

quote: A good goal to set for your project is to have 50% of your tags come from global tags.
fact: The goal for a Dovetail research project is that half of its tags come from GitLab global tags.

quote: Calculate Priority Score: Multiply the three scores (max score = 125)
fact: Critical experience priority is business criticality times user impact times measurability, each 1-5, for a max of 125.

quote: "Everyone With Access" sounds like it means _everyone_, but on GitLab.com it actually means _everyone with a GitLab account_.
fact: On GitLab.com the Pages setting 'Everyone With Access' means anyone with a GitLab account; fully public prototypes need the 'Everyone' setting.

quote: Color contrast issues where the contrast is lower than 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for graphic elements.
fact: Dark mode reviews flag contrast below 4.5:1 for text or 3:1 for graphic elements.

quote: The program duration is 15 weeks.
fact: The Tufts University capstone course GitLab volunteers support lasts 15 weeks, with student groups of 4-5.

quote: I expect a clear **DACI**, with exactly one approver and exactly one DRI.
fact: Manav expects decisions to have a DACI with exactly one approver and one DRI.
